docs.title: LLMBench
docs.text:
Reproducible evaluation, benchmarking and regression testing for non-deterministic LLM and RAG systems.

LLMBench runs every (model, prompt, sample) combination several times and scores quality, consistency, failure rate, latency and cost. Every comparison then comes with confidence intervals, a named statistical test and an effect size, plus a CI gate that fails only on regressions you can trust.

  • Interactive dashboard: explore the demo results, or connect your own API to launch and compare benchmarks from the browser.
  • Live demo report — a full HTML report regenerated by CI on every push (mock provider, illustrative numbers, $0).
  • Demo comparisons, safety suite and RAG sweep
  • Methodology — every metric and statistical method with formulas.
  • Architecture and design decisions
  • RAG evaluation and CI eval gate
  • Source code: github.com/PiyushDas-2004/LLM-Bench

docs.title: Quickstart (no API keys, no cost)
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/PiyushDas-2004/LLM-Bench.git && cd LLM-Bench
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -e .
llmbench run examples/quickstart.yaml
llmbench report latest

docs.title: LLMBench architecture
docs.text: This document describes how LLMBench is put together: its layers, the path of one llmbench run, the data model, what each module is responsible for, the invariants the code relies on, and where it can be extended. Design rationale for individual decisions lives in the ADRs; statistical definitions live in METHODOLOGY.md. Module paths are relative to src/llmbench/.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: LLMBench evaluates non-deterministic LLM and RAG systems reproducibly. An experiment is a grid of models x prompts x dataset samples x repeated trials. LLMBench executes the grid against providers under rate limits, retries and a budget, records every trial, computes metrics (lexical, structural, semantic, consistency, operational, safety, RAG, LLM-judge), reports per-configuration estimates with cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals, compares runs with paired tests, and turns a comparison into a CI gate (llmbench check, see CI_EVAL_GATE.md).

The one rule enforced by tooling is the provider-SDK boundary (see Invariants).

docs.title: Sequence of llmbench run
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant U as User
    participant C as cli.run / _execute
    participant P as runner.prepare
    participant R as Runner workers
    participant K as ResponseCache
    participant B as BudgetGuard
    participant L as CircuitBreaker + RateLimiter
    participant V as Provider
    participant S as RunStore
    participant E as metrics.engine.evaluate_run
    participant J as LLMJudge
    U->>C: llmbench run experiment.yaml
    C->>P: load_experiment + prepare (dataset, sampling, task, prompts, availability, pricing)
    C->>C: plan.estimate; exit 2 if over cost_confirm_threshold_usd without --yes
    C->>R: Runner.run(config) with SIGINT -> request_stop
    R->>S: create_run(manifest, dataset_hash, n_expected)
    loop each missing WorkItem (trial-major, `concurrency` workers)
        R->>K: get(provider, request, model params + base_url)
        alt cache hit
            K-->>R: GenerationResult (cached)
        else miss
            R->>B: reserve(estimated cost)
            loop attempts until success, non-retryable error or max_attempts
                R->>L: breaker.acquire, limiter.acquire(rpm, tpm)
                R->>V: generate(request) under wait_for(timeout_s)
                V-->>R: result or ProviderError(ErrorClass, Retry-After)
            end
            R->>B: settle(actual cost)
            R->>K: put (successful results only)
        end
        R->>S: add_trial(TrialRecord) checkpoint
    end
    R->>S: refresh_run_totals
    R->>E: evaluate_run(store, run_id)
    E->>S: trials, dataset hash check
    E->>J: pointwise judgments (if llm_judge_correctness)
    J->>S: add_judge_call (every call)
    E->>S: replace_metric_values
    R->>S: update_run(status, stop_reason)
    C->>S: summarize_run (cluster-bootstrap CIs, Pareto)
    C-->>U: summary table, optional --report HTML

Exit codes of llmbench run: 0 when the run completed or was interrupted (it prints the resume command), 1 on a configuration or lookup error, 2 when the estimate exceeds cost_confirm_threshold_usd without --yes, 3 when the run ended budget_exceeded or partial.
